newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe opens "world largest" tobacco sales floor.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe opens "world largest" tobacco sales floor.

text.p: A black Zimbabwean businessman on Tuesday opened what he said was the world's largest flue-cured tobacco auction floors.

The Z$210 million ($18.6 million) Boka Tobacco Auction Floors opening coincided with the start of the southern African country's annual sales of the yellow leaf which is one of Zimbabwe's top foreign exchange earners.

Owned by Roger Boka -- who has in the past accused white commercial farmers of frustrating efforts by the country's majority blacks to break into the tobacco industry -- the new floors are Zimbabwe's third after the Burley Tobacco and the Tobacco Sales Floors owned mainly by white commercial farmers.
Boka said his floors measure 30,000 square metres and have the capacity to handle 380 million kg (836 million lbs) of tobacco making it the world's largest auction for flue-cured tobacco
Opening the floors, Agriculture Minister Dennis Norman hailed the project as the country's biggest local investment since Zimbabwe's independence from Britain in 1980.
Boka, whose business interests include a merchant bank and gold mines, told reporters he had managed to secure $1.2 billion to finance the country's entire 1997 tobacco crop of 214 million kg.
